correctness.rationale: The autonomous product heading chain has uniform stationary law and mean drift −2g. The two-sided stationary workload is the supremum of integrated past velocities; the negative ergodic drift also makes workloads driven by the same future coalesce at a boundary encounter, proving uniqueness. The tilted generator is a Kronecker sum of two two-state tilts plus −2gλI; the largest eigenvalue is the stated radical expression minus s+2gλ. It leaves zero with slope −2g, is strictly convex and eventually positive for v>g, yielding a unique positive zero and a strictly positive eigenvector h. Multiplication over the four sign choices gives the cubic determinant (see independent replay). Its coefficients, split at v=√2g and 2g, have just one sign change. The three inward phases have transient killed generator Q_UU, so the stated inverse gives positive atom masses; summing the interior equation gives 1ᵀWh=0 and supplies the missing outward boundary balance in Qᵀm=Wh. Integration by parts with the reflected generator then proves exactly a single exponential plus an atom after normalization, not only a tail asymptotic. At each fixed λ>0, strict convexity in the rates orders the tilted eigenvalues by imbalance and reverses the order of positive roots; equal rates give the stated upper bound. In the rare-flipper limit the roots are bounded by that bound. When v<2g the limiting radical function is strictly negative at a point between zero and its positive root, keeping the roots bounded away from zero; solving the limiting equation then gives s(2g−v)/[2g(v−g)]. For v≥2g the limiting function is strictly positive at every λ>0. Grouping the p-terms in the cubic and dividing by λ² at v=2g or by λ at v>2g gives the stated square-root and linear scales. Replay: python /workspace/audit_evidence/reconstruct.py (fluid_determinant), only for cubic algebra.
residual_risks: All rates are strictly positive prior to the limit; no result about uniqueness at the exactly frozen endpoint or about the absolute center of mass.

value.rationale: At fixed total flip rate the theorem identifies the unique fastest conditional separation decay, and for a nearly frozen swimmer locates the change from positive limiting confinement exponent to collapse. The square-root and linear laws distinguish the critical and supercritical physical regimes quantitatively; the already-known exponential structure alone does not have that value.
residual_risks: The exponent measures positive-gap binding length, not by itself the unconditional contact fraction; the zero-rate endpoint is a limit, not a separate invariant-law theorem.
